jobs.description: Company DescriptionAt METRO, we’re more than a global food wholesaler. We are ONE METRO: a diverse team of over 85,000 colleagues across more than 30 countries, united by one mission: enabling our 15 million customers to create meaningful moments in hospitality and independent trade.We shape the M with passion, commitment, and growth mindset. This means taking on responsibility, making our company your company and creating a business together that remains true to its roots but always seeks new solutions.Job DescriptionThe Corporate Security, Safety and Forensics team has a vital role in protecting people and assets at METRO. The team is responsible for dealing with security risks as well as possible violations of laws and regulations, both nationally and internationally. It carries out security assessments, security audits, and fraud investigations. It creates appropriate guidelines and audit mechanisms and coordinates the regional and local Security managers. In the event of suspected violations of laws or internal regulations, the team investigates the incidents and reports to the senior management. In addition, the corporate safety function ensures a safe working environment by developing and monitoring company-wide safety standards and preventive measures. The Corporate Security, Safety and Forensics team is part of the Audit, Asset Protection & Governance division. You will support the team in two areas, security and forensics.Your tasks:- Loss Prevention: Support initiatives aimed at reducing shrinkage, protecting company assets, and strengthening operational resilience.- Incident Management: Oversee and coordinate security incidents, liaising with emergency services and authorities as needed, and manage, maintain, and develop the security incident management system.- Crisis Management: Support and coordinate the crisis management process, including maintaining crisis management guidelines, designing and delivering training, and conducting security risk assessments for current and prospective operations.- Risk Assessment: Continuously monitor and evaluate evolving threat landscapes, providing recommendations to mitigate emerging risks.- policies, and perform OSINT background checks to support corporate integrity and compliance objectives.- Investigations & Event Security: Conduct fraud investigations, interviews, and analyze physical The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-/part-time position (38.5/19.5 hours per week)  is to be filled as soon as possible in the Institute for Hygiene and Public Health, Section Global Child Health of the University Hospital Bonn:Scientific coordinator (m/f/d)The Section of Global Child Health was established in November 2025 with the appointment of the Endowed Professorship in Global Child Health. The Section’s remit includes research and teaching in Germany and internationally, as well as clinical practice and the applied, practice-oriented engagement with global health challenges affecting children and adolescents. The professorship is structured as a tandem appointment with a corresponding position at the University of Malawi, based in Lilongwe.You will work in close collaboration with the section head in establishing sound research and communication networks with partners in Malawi and GermanyThe professorship focuses on research in the area of neonatal, child, and adolescent health in “Low and Middle Income Countries” (LMICs), identifies barriers to and solutions for improving global child health, and facilitates the transfer of epidemiological and clinical evidence into health care services with the goal of improving the health status of all children globally.It facilitates institutional, national and international networking and collaboration with universities, academic institutions and key development partners.In addition, it provides academic and health policy advice to national and international governmental as well as non-governmental organizations with regard to global child health.The position is initially limited to three years and remunerated according to TV-L EG 13 (German tax ID is a prerequisite). If you currently live abroad, you should be willing to relocate to Germany temporarily. Subject to interest and feasibility, a temporary increase in the scope of employment through third-party funded resources is envisaged.Tasks:This position offers the opportunity to actively contribute to the development of global strategies for improving children's health and to build and design a completely new international research and education structure.- Strategic coordination and management of international research, education and clinical programmes across the two professorships and the EKFS network- Planning, coordination, and monitoring of cross-institutional activities with academic and non-academic partners- Management of communication channels between institutions, disciplines, and countries, ensuring efficient information flow and alignment of activities- Coordination, and implementation of training materials and structured capacity-building programmes in collaboration with international experts- Planning, organisation, and delivery of international workshops and seminars in online and on-site formats- Preparation of annual progress and impact reports, dissemination of results through conferences and other scientific communication formats- Contribution to the strategic development, coordination, and drafting of third-party funding proposals to expand and sustain programme activitiesRequirements:- A full academic degree at Master’s level or higher in a health-related discipline- A strong interest in global child health and international health systems cooperation- Demonstrated experience in project coordination and research management- Excellent organisational skills and a structured, meticulous approach to work- Proven ability to navigate academic hierarchies and university administrative processes, combined with sensitivity to intercultural contexts- Strong teamwork skills, resilience, and the ability to assert and represent set positions- Full professional proficiency in both German and English, written and spoken Willingness to maintain an appropriate on-site presence at the university in Bonn- Previous extended study, research, or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country would be considered a strong assetWe offer: An interesting and challenging job in a modern research institution with attractive research infrastructures and a cooperative and communicative institute culture. This includes:- **Responsible and diverse: **A position with significant scope for initiative and development within a truly collegial and supportive team- **Fair compensation: **Pay according to the TV-L collective agreement, including annual bonus and company pension scheme- **Family-friendly flexibility: **Flexible working time models, access to a place in our company daycare center, and programs supporting employees returning from parental leave- **Smart commuting: **Excellent connection to the SWB public transport network and the option of an interest-free loan for the purchase of an e-bike- **Supported development: **Individual training opportunities through courses, e-learning programs, and coaching sessions- **Structured onboarding: **A systematic introduction to your new role and team- **Healthy at work: **A wide range of health and wellness programs, plus free membership at the UKB fitness studio- **Employee benefits: **Access to discounted offers for employees (corporate benefits)We are committed to diversity and equal opportunities. Our goal is to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are underrepresented and to particularly promote their careers. We therefore urge relevantly qualified women to apply. Applications are treated in accordance with the State Equal Opportunities Act. Applications from suitable people with proven severe disabilities and those of equal status are particularly welcome.How to apply:If you are seeking a challenging and internationally oriented position within a leading research and clinical environment, we would be pleased to hear from you. For further information, please feel free to contact us.Please submit your complete application documents by 28/02/2026, quoting the vacancy reference number [ST-37032], as a single PDF file (maximum size 5 MB), by email to the address below.English is the working language in many areas of the position; sound knowledge of German is required for administrative issues. Support services for international applicants may be available, including guidance on visa and residence matters as well as initial orientation and integration. Information on dual career options and local infrastructure can be provided upon request.Prof. Dr. med. jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day As a commodity management professional (f/m/d) you are the strategic procurement owner of the respective commodities within Gas Services Central Service Business. Role requires individual to develop and align a resilient Ecosystem strategy together with commodity circles and in line with global SE strategy and Global Service Operations (GSO & its Regions) objectives. Typical day for Commodity Management professional includes provide and demonstrate supply market knowledge beyond Procurement perspectives to generate value and impact, negotiation with suppliers, supplier relationship management, business case and sourcing strategy preparation/execution, reporting, problem solving, supply chain risk mitigation  as well as alignment meetings with internal/external x-functional team. How You’ll Make an Impact* Develop and execute Comprehensive Commodity Strategies (forward-looking) aimed at achieving business objectives (Growth, Resilience & Cost Out) for Global Service Operations & the Regions * Lead Cross functional Commodity Circle Team that embodies “Value Creation” mindset and drives improvements in cost, on-time delivery, quality, and lead times, while ensuring adequate capacity. The successful candidate will be the strategic leader for assigned commodities.  * Provide strategic vision and represents their respective business interests into a global commodity team. Act as a role model for ownership, innovation, and transformation aligned with Siemens Energy’s values and strategy; Lead and develop assigned team members in commodity. * Works on commodity structure and provide periodic updates of commodity health to Strategic Procurement leadership and key customers, shares supplier market intelligence across Siemens Energy; Define and implement negotiation concepts and strategies to maximize savings; negotiate frame contracts and price lists * Supplier Management: Supplier selection, incl. documentation/onboarding and communication of strategic suppliers. Strategic evaluations, supplier classifications and supplier development to ensure an optimum supply chain.* Handle relationships with strategic suppliers to ensure alignment with company demands, enabling early supplier involvement and driving cost-out initiatives; Identify procurement risks and opportunities through supplier market analysis and scouting, integrating findings into ecosystem strategies for continuous improvement of managed spend.What You Bring* Bachelor's or Master's Degree, or equivalent experience in Business, Supply Chain Management, Engineering or related field; long term of work experience in the procurement area and a proven track record, ideally in a global organization* Strong commercial and technical understanding and knowledge of procurement, project management, and international contract law* Experience in functional leadership and project management is required* Long term experience in multinational Procurement/ Supply Chain function* Fluent language skills in English(primary) and German(secondary) languageAbout the TeamIn our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more.Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbaticalWe value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

We are looking for a Customer Advisor to join our international team in Copenhagen. Our new Customer Advisor will support both the UK and the Dutch markets, delivering unparalleled and timely support that keeps our customers delighted. Through providing support and guidance, you empower our customers to use Famly effectively. As the first point of contact for customer inquiries, you play a key role in ensuring customer satisfaction and customer loyalty 🎯

As a Customer Advisor at Famly , you are responsible for delivering human support that's actually human. You're catching us at an inflection point with the fundamental nature of customer advisory evolving before our eyes.

With AI handling routine queries, the days of being a librarian pointing to the right shelf are over; we are now looking for detectives. You will empower our customers to use Famly effectively by stepping in precisely where the automation ends, tackling the complex, technical edge cases that require deep forensic analysis. This role is not for those seeking the rhythm of repetitive quick wins; it is for resilient puzzle solvers ready to navigate the hardest questions our customers can ask.

You’ll be joining 18 other teammates who support markets across the world. Together, you’ll make sure that all customers have a first-class experience when contacting Famly. You’ll also be working closely with our Customer Success team, who help our customers get started on the platform, as well as our Key Account Managers, who handle the accounts of the larger organisations using Famly.

•

Track and report customer feedback and issues to improve product or service quality.

jobs.occupation: Senior Partnership Advisor, Foundations & Private Sector (Re-advertisement)
jobs.description:
The overall purpose of Danish Red Cross’ (DRC) international engagement is to increase and strengthen humanitarian impact, inspire and act for human dignity, and enhance resilience and social cohesion in contexts of poverty, conflict and disaster.

The Global Partnership unit leads the coordination and strategic direction of the Danish Red Cross’ international partnerships, external and within the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement. The Unit is responsible for global resource mobilization efforts and initiatives and provides support to countries and regions. The Unit hosts the Danish Red Cross’ core donor specialization knowledge and capacity on compliance and strategies. Furthermore, the unit supports and quality assures proposals to core donors.

The position

As part of the Movement relations and private partnerships team (MOPS), the Partnership Advisor will drive Danish Red Cross’ strategic engagement with Danish and international foundations and private sector actors, with the objective of growing and diversifying non-institutional funding and strategic partnerships. The role combines new partnership development with strategic management and growth of high-value, multi-year partnerships. It focuses on senior-level relationship building, development of innovative partnership models, negotiation of multi-year agreements, and strong partnership stewardship across the full lifecycle. The Advisor will position DRC as a preferred humanitarian partner among Danish businesses, corporate foundations, family foundations, and selected international private sector actors through collaboration within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

Main responsibilities:

• Develop and implement a multi-year strategy for Danish and international private sector and foundation engagement aligned with DRC’s international priorities.

• Build and convert a qualified pipeline of high-value partnership opportunities, with clear income and partnership-growth ambitions.

• Lead the strategic management of one or more high-value, multi-year foundation partnerships, including relationship management, governance, internal coordination, delivery oversight and identification of opportunities for growth.

• Ensure strong partnership stewardship throughout the grant lifecycle, working closely with programme, finance and operational colleagues to support delivery, reporting, compliance and proactive management of risks and partner expectations.

• Develop partnership models beyond traditional grant funding, including strategic co-creation and multi-stakeholder alliances.

• Support country and regional teams to identify, shape and pursue high-potential private sector and foundation partnerships.

• Work closely with Business Development Advisors, Fundraising, and Operations to align private sector engagement with programming priorities.

• Represent DRC in relevant private sector and foundation networks and relevant Movement platforms related to private sector engagement.

We expect you to have the following qualifications:

• A master’s degree or MBA in Business, International Affairs, International Development or related

• Significant experience (7-10 years) in business development, resource mobilization, partnership development, preferably in the humanitarian or non-profit sector

• Demonstrated success in securing high-value, multi-year private sector or foundation partnerships

• Demonstrated experience managing complex, high-value, multi-year and/or multi-stakeholder partnerships including stakeholder engagement, negotiation, renewal and growth

• Strong established network in Denmark and ideally internationally

• Solid understanding of private sector CSR strategies, corporate foundations, and philanthropic trends

• Strong strategic account-management skills, including experience balancing partner expectations with organisational priorities and operational realities

• Experience coordinating complex partnerships across multiple internal teams, technical areas and geographies

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, Danish is an advantage

As a person you have the following competences:

• High level of strategic thinking and diplomatic and political judgement

• Ability to lead processes and engage people across functions and geographies

• Results-oriented and entrepreneurial mindset and ability to turn opportunities into concrete action.

• Collaborative team player with the ability to build trust and work in a multicultural environment

We offer

A full-time position of 37 working hours per week in an inspiring workplace. You will have the opportunity to work in a diversified motivated team of donor experts and be part of Danish Red Cross’ large global humanitarian action. You will refer to the Head of Global Partnership in Copenhagen.

The position is based in Copenhagen with potential 4-8-week travel. Salary and employment conditions will comply with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargain agreement with AC.

Application and further information

We look forward to receiving your application via the Red Cross home page www.rodekors.dk/job

In case you have questions to the position please contact Head of Global Partnerships, Marie-Chantal Legendre Dahl mcd@rodekors.dk or Team coordinator Vivian Pucher vipuc@rodekors.dk

Application deadline is 20th November 2026; Interviews will take place soon thereafter. The expected date of commencement is as soon as possible, preferably no later than January 1st.

_

Red Cross

Join us. Together we can make a world of difference. The Red Cross is always present. We are the largest humanitarian organisation in the world and for 150 years we have helped alleviate people through wars and disasters, diseases and loneliness. Most countries have signed an agreement which gives the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement a unique position and mandate to provide aid regardless of nationality, race or political views. We currently count 11 million volunteers in 191 countries. We are part of your local community no matter where you live. When disaster strikes, we are there._

Copenhagen, Denmark Do you want to work with data engineering, platform development, and data-based automated processes within Saxo's Financial Crime Prevention (FCP)? About the job Saxo is an investment bank with high speed, global colleagues, and a strong focus on using technology and data to prevent financial crime. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the FCP Modelling & Development team. FCP Modelling & Development is part of the 1st Line of Defence in Group Operations and is located in Saxo's headquarters in Hellerup. The team works with models and data-based automated processes used across FCP. The goal is to ensure that these data assets and processes are sound, fit for purpose, adequately documented, secure, and regularly reviewed. Responsibilities Build, operate, and continuously improve reusable AML data products, data-modelling components, and user-facing interfaces, with clear ownership, lineage, documentation, quality controls, and production reliability. Design robust ETL pipelines and integration interfaces for operational, analytical, model-development, and external-platform use cases, enabling secure and efficient data exchange across internal and external systems. Translate FCP and AML requirements into durable, adaptable production systems, contributing to solution architecture decisions on design patterns, system scalability, regulatory compliance, and flexibility across AML processes. Partner with FCP and AML subject-matter experts on transaction monitoring, customer segmentation, scenario development, client risk rating, surveillance support, and AML-related development initiatives that strengthen financial crime prevention capabilities. Define automated checks for completeness, consistency, validity, reconciliation, source-to-target integrity, architectural integrity, security, performance, and governance standards. Own observability, alerting, alerting, incident response, backfills, runbooks, performance tuning, production support, and operational resilience for critical data assets. Raise engineering standards through design and code reviews, mentoring, reusable patterns, clean and well-documented code, test-driven development, secure coding practices, CI/CD pipeline optimization, automated testing, and continuous improvement. What you bring 5+ years of experience in data engineering, software engineering, or a related production data role. Strong Python, SQL, and Spark skills, with experience building and maintaining production data pipelines and data models. **WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the teams by creating or helping create great guest experiences, and use every day as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer or staff member; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of people who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You'll learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path—our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The Global Talent Management Lead is responsible for setting the standard for how JOE identifies, develops and moves talent, ensuring that internal mobility and leadership readiness are predictable, data-driven and scalable across the organization. The role owns the talent review and development planning approach for operational and office-based roles, the talent management system and pipeline reporting, and partners with Culture, Performance & Reward, Operations, People Business Partners and regional T&LD to shape decisions on where and how talent is built. As part of the Talent & Leadership Development team within People & Development, this position is critical to the ambition of filling 90% of leadership roles from within, supporting JOE's purpose and growth ambitions.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Set the company-wide standard for talent development, owning a regular and objective talent review process for operational and office-based roles, anchored in individual development plans.

• Shape and own the roll-out of the talent development model, starting with operational roles from Juicer to Store Manager and scaling quickly to office-based roles, with SOPs that work consistently across all regions.

• Own the strategy, selection and implementation of the talent management system, ensuring it connects with shared learning platforms and provides one source of truth for talent data.

• Own pipeline reporting and insight - internal fill rate, successor coverage, development plan completion and employee development experience - informing strategic people and growth decisions at leadership level.

• Ensure pipeline gaps are identified early and closed across all regions, steering gap-closing actions with People Business Partners and regional T&LD.

• Own visible career pathways and promotion criteria across the organization, so employees can see their next step from day one.

• Partner with Culture, Performance & Reward and Operations to set aligned leadership standards, competency framework and people cycle, acting as the organization's thought leader on talent development.

• Contribute to pipeline-fill initiatives, such as structured mentoring, that turn talent review outcomes into concrete development actions.

**WHO YOU ARE

**

• Passionate about developing talent. A standard-setter who builds career pathways and talent development processes that work the same way in every region and every role

• Data-led: you turn pipeline numbers into insight that leaders act on

• Operationally credible: you understand how careers are built from the bar to the office

• A partner who influences across Culture, Performance & Reward, Operations, People Business Partners and regional T&LD without needing authority

• A thought leader who works with high autonomy and shapes how we build leaders

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• 7+ years in talent management, talent development or people development roles, ideally in global multi-site quick service restaurant, retail or similar front line heavy industry

• Proven track record owning talent review-, succession planning- and individual development plan processes

• Experience selecting and implementing a talent management system, incl. integration with learning platforms

• Strong analytical skills: pipeline reporting, internal fill rate and successor coverage

• Experience designing competency frameworks, career pathways and promotion criteria

• Experience rolling out global processes and SOPs across regions and markets

• Fluent in English - other languages are a bonus

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

**Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

****ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, GCP Inspection Office, R&D Quality
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**R&D Quality encompasses four teams GCLP/GLP Quality, PV Quality, Audit Calibration, Quality and GCP Quality. R&D Quality has a large range of stakeholders, and we have an important role in delivering our 2030 vision to transform the future of cancer treatment.

In the role as AD GCP Inspection Office you will be driving day-to-day GCP Quality activities including audit together with a dedicated and highly skilled team. Furthermore, you will be taking up the role as GCP Inspection QA lead.

The role requires profound understanding of how the GCP requirements are applied into practice, especially with focus on the European requirements and interpretation of ICH GCP R3 and Computerized Systems in Clinical Trials.

The role includes hands on GCP Quality activities such as support to our many stakeholders as well as performing audits alone or together with own team members or with support from neighbouring teams. You become a key member of the R&D Quality leadership team that together drives people engagement, setting strategies and ensuring R&D Quality deliverables.

The role requires strong collaboration capabilities in an international setting across various QA departments as well across the company with target stakeholders such as Clinical Trial Operations, Clinical Data, Integration & Reporting, Digital Development, Medical, GDS&PV, and Regulatory Affairs.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Reporting to Director and Team Lead Inspection Office R&D Quality

• It will ensure GCP inspection readiness across cross functional clinical -study team.

• The role oversees end-of-end inspection planning and execution including logistics and stakeholder coordination.

• Lead and oversee GCP inspection readiness/preparation activities and serve as an inspection lead for regulatory health authority inspection including but not limited to US FDA, MHRA, EMA, CFDI, PMDA etc.

• Collaborate with the cross functional clinical study teams to develop and execute and integrated risk-based inspection readiness/preparation strategy ensuring consistent alignment across functions.

• Manage end to end inspection readiness/preparation activities, including development and maintenance of inspection storyboards with the SMEs, proactive identification and mitigation of the inspection related risk and planning, facilitation.

• Lead the mock inspections for high-risk trials across Genmab locations.

• During the inspection coordinate and assign inspection requests to appropriate SMEs providing oversight and appropriate SME, also guide to ensure timely and effective responses.

• Create/revise appropriate tools / SOPs for inspection readiness/preparation and management.

• Ensure Veeva records are updated for inspection records or related records.

• Demonstrate ability to solve complex problems requiring in-depth evaluation of various factors.

• Fulfill inspection commitments and respond to the inspection and carry out post inspection activities.

• Maintain a central repository of global inspection status and updates

• Meticulous attention to detail, excellent review skills and ability to independently manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

• Support/manage site inspection in collaboration with GCP Quality.

• Lead and facilitate post-inspection lessons learned session to trends, share best practices and drive sustainable process improvements.

**Requirements

**

• MS, or BS or similar in Natural Science

• 10+ years of experience in a GCP Quality function or similar

• Deep expertise in GCP processes and the EMA, PMDA and FDA requirements.

• Demonstrated leadership in regulatory inspections and health authority interactions.

• Considered to be a Domain Expert within GCP by peers with a strong interest and ability to educate others

• Experience as Lead Auditor within GCP is an advantage

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK732.768,00---1.099.152,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Job title: Senior Research Scientist – Discovery Pharmacology

Department: Global Research

Location: Måløv, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Senior Research Scientist – Discovery Pharmacology, you will help build a new interdisciplinary team in Global Research that generates and validates therapeutic concepts in cardiometabolic disease and healthspan. You will combine hands-on rodent pharmacology with original scientific thinking, shaping research questions and turning emerging biology into opportunities for drug discovery. Your work will bring new projects into the early discovery pipeline, because lasting health starts with the science we build today.

What you will bring

You hold a PhD in pharmacology, physiology, neuroscience or a related discipline, or bring equivalent relevant research experience. You also bring:

• At least two years of relevant post-PhD experience with scientific innovation, or equivalent scientific contributions.

• Hands-on experience in rodent pharmacology.

• Strong skills in experimental design, quantitative analysis and interpretation of complex biological data.

• Scientific depth in metabolic physiology, neuroscience, in vitro pharmacology, or a related area.

• Original scientific thinking, intellectual curiosity and the ability to turn ideas into testable hypotheses.

• A collaborative approach and the ability to work independently while contributing to shared research goals.

• Clear scientific communication in written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience in metabolic phenotyping, advanced behavioural assays, rodent surgery, modern neuroscience methods, in vitro or ex vivo approaches, or developing novel experimental technologies. We welcome complementary profiles – you are not expected to bring expertise in every method or scientific area.

What you will do

You will contribute to both the scientific direction and hands-on experimental work of the team. Your responsibilities will include:

• Generate hypotheses and propose new therapeutic concepts grounded in biological understanding.

• Design, conduct, analyse and interpret mouse and rat pharmacology studies to investigate efficacy, mechanism of action and physiological responses.

• Develop experimental models and introduce methodologies that enable us to address challenging scientific questions.

• Connect in vivo findings with relevant in vitro and ex vivo experiments.

• Integrate evidence into recommendations on how emerging concepts should advance, change direction or be discontinued.

• Document and communicate findings, sharing scientific insights across disciplines and project teams.

• Contribute to rigorous, reproducible experimental practice and high standards of animal welfare.

All scientists are expected to contribute directly to experimental work alongside laboratory technicians and fellow scientists.

Who you will work with

You will join a new interdisciplinary team in Global Research within Research & Development, combining expertise in physiology, pharmacology, neuroscience and molecular innovation. Day to day, you will work closely with scientists and laboratory technicians. The team, headed by Christoffer Clemmensen, is currently recruiting at multiple levels, so you contribute to shape the new team from the onset.

You are expected to establish close collaborations across the organisation with colleagues in chemistry, biology, DMPK and relevant technology functions to develop and test new therapeutic concepts. Bringing these perspectives together early helps the team make clear, evidence-based decisions at pace.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to shape the research of a new team and contribute your own ideas, in an environment that values thoughtful scientific challenge, collaboration and learning from unexpected findings.

Your impact begins here

As Senior Clinical Genetics Data Scientist, you will turn human genetic evidence into clear recommendations that guide clinical development decisions. You will lead defined projects that combine trial and population genetic data with clinical outcomes and molecular measurements. Your work will help explain disease biology, understand why people respond differently to treatment and identify where patient stratification, or asset differentiation could matter. It helps teams decide with confidence, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You are an independent, systematic scientist with sound judgement, who communicates uncertainty openly, acts on feedback and sees work through to its outcome.

• A PhD in statistical genetics, genetic epidemiology, bioinformatics or a related quantitative discipline; or a relevant master’s degree with equivalent demonstrated research and applied experience.

• Demonstrated independent ownership of complex human genetics projects, from study design and data preparation to robust interpretation and communication of results.

• Strong, hands-on experience in GWAS design, execution and interpretation, including linkage disequilibrium, population structure, relatedness, multiple testing, power and validation.

• Proficiency in R and/or Python, Linux and genetics tools such as PLINK, BCFtools, GATK, REGENIE, SAIGE or equivalent, with reproducible programming, version control, documentation and quality review.

• Practical experience processing SNP array and WGS data, including quality control, genotype harmonisation, phasing and imputation, variant calling, filtering and functional annotation.

• Hands-on experience conducting and interpreting pQTL analyses, including cis and trans mapping, multiple-testing control and integration with GWAS or colocalisation evidence.

• The ability to coordinate stakeholders, manage project risks and dependencies, and present complex findings clearly in English to audiences with different technical backgrounds.

Desirable, but not essential:

Experience in clinical trial genetics, pharmacogenetics or clinical development, particularly in cardiometabolic, obesity or renal disease; rare-variant and gene-based tests, genetic risk prediction or advanced causal inference; or work with secure cloud computing, biobank-scale resources and regulated analytical environments.

What you’ll do

You will own project outcomes from the scientific question to validated results and practical recommendations.

• Plan and run GWAS, pQTL and related analyses of disease phenotypes, clinical endpoints, biomarkers and treatment response, using trial and external cohort data.

• Prepare SNP array and whole-genome sequencing data into analysis-ready datasets, and use fine-mapping, colocalisation and causal inference to prioritise plausible variants, genes, pathways and biomarkers.

• Investigate pharmacogenetic associations and genetically informed subgroups, separating prognostic signals from evidence of differential treatment benefit.

• Turn findings into decision-focused reports and presentations, with clear uncertainty and limitations, and contribute genetics content to publications and regulatory documents.

• Build documented, version-controlled workflows, mentor colleagues through code review and feedback, and use genetic and clinical data within approved consent, governance and quality requirements.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Clinical Omics Sciences, part of Translational & Clinical Omics in Research & Development. Here, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing, bringing together curiosity, data, technology and collaboration.

Your closest partners will be Clinical Development Teams, translational scientists, human genetics researchers, biostatisticians, data managers and data engineers. You will also coordinate agreed work with external collaborators and suppliers. You will explain your technical choices in accessible language, build alignment on the question, deliverables and decision, and speak up early when something stalls.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to determine and execute the analytical approach for your projects, within agreed objectives and quality requirements. You will be supported to perform at your best, make your voice heard and grow through practical project experience, scientific feedback and relevant learning offerings. You will also help raise the standard for the whole team by shaping shared workflows, templates and methods.

Are you passionate about renewable energy and eager to work at the forefront of the global energy transition? PEAK Wind is seeking a Structural Engineer Consultant to support Wind Turbine (WTG) and Balance of Plant (BoP) engineering on offshore wind projects, with a focus on Wind Turbine Components, jacket foundation design, scour and scour protection, and cable mechanical engineering.

Introducing the WTG & BoP Engineering Team

You will become part of our WTG & BoP Engineering team, where we work collaboratively to support renewable energy projects around the world. Our team consists of highly motivated professionals who bring diverse backgrounds and a strong commitment to excellence. We support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate both individual and collective achievements.

You will report to the Head of WTG & BoP Engineering and work closely with colleagues across different areas, bringing your perspective to a collaborative and purposeful team environment.

How You Will Make an Impact

As a Structural Engineer Consultant, you will contribute to the successful development, construction, and operation of our clients’ wind projects. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Supporting End of Warranties activities, technical due diligence, and asset management topics for clients throughout the development, construction, and operational phases of wind farms.

• Providing engineering expertise across both WTG and BoP systems, including turbine components, jacket foundations, scour protection, inter-array and export cables, offshore substations, and associated infrastructure.

• Leading the engineering activities related to foundation, scour protection, and cable work packages for offshore wind projects, from development and procurement through construction and into operations.

• Acting as a trusted technical advisor on jacket foundation design and scour management, reviewing foundation and scour protection solutions from design basis through detailed design, installation, and monitoring to ensure safe, robust, and cost-effective performance.

• Providing cable mechanical engineering support, including inter-array and export cable routing, burial and protection, cable protection systems, crossings, and the cable - foundation interface.

• Identifying, assessing, and mitigating technical risks related to turbine components, foundations, scour, cables, and asset integrity, and maintaining the project technical risk register.

• Following up on the certification process and managing interfaces with certification bodies to ensure that designs and deliverables meet the relevant standards and requirements.

• Contributing to the development of best practices and knowledge sharing across PEAK Wind’s offshore engineering services.

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

At PEAK Wind, we know success comes in many forms. What matters most is your mindset, curiosity, and drive to make an impact. The following qualities and experiences will help you succeed in this role:

• A degree in a relevant field such as Mechanical, Structural, Civil, Geotechnical, or Offshore Engineering, or similar.

• A minimum of 5 years post-education professional experience in offshore wind, the wider offshore industry, or another complex environment.

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written.

• A structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to take initiative.

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to thrive in an international, cross - functional team.

• Solid understanding of WTG components, including their function, common failure modes, and repair methodologies

• Solid understanding of the offshore wind foundation design process, particularly for jacket structures, including the impact of scour and the design of scour protection.

• Knowledge of subsea cable systems and cable mechanical engineering, such as burial and protection, cable protection systems, crossings, and the cable - foundation interface.

• Good knowledge of offshore wind EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) as well as O&M (Operations and Maintenance), including how design and installation choices affect long - term operation of the asset.

• Familiarity with offshore wind industry standards and certification frameworks, such as DNV standards, IEC, IECRE, and Eurocodes.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to work on leading renewable energy projects alongside experienced industry professionals

• Flexible working arrangements that support both your career and personal life

• A flat organisational structure where your ideas are welcomed and your contributions matter

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Job Title: Tech Lead

Department: Quality AI & Data Enterprise IT & Quality

Location: Ballerup, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Tech Lead, you will shape the architecture behind AI and data across Novo Quality processes. You will turn business priorities into a technical roadmap, guide the move to Databricks and make sure AI applications are built on trusted, high-quality data. Staying close to the implementation, you will help engineers build systems that work in real life and stand up in a regulated GxP environment. Your impact will be felt in stronger quality processes and faster progress.

What you’ll bring

A relevant university degree, and the hands-on technical depth to lead delivery of AI and data systems.

•     Experience with Databricks and AWS or Azure.

•     Experience leading the technical delivery of production systems, while staying close enough to the implementation to see where designs succeed or fail.

•     Strong software engineering skills and experience designing systems across data processing, APIs, integrations and applications.

•     Practical understanding of data engineering, including data modelling, pipelines, data quality and the consequences of upstream changes for downstream users.

•     Hands-on experience building with LLMs, and the ability to assess agent architectures, retrieval approaches, tool integrations and evaluation strategies.

•     The ability to make decisions across the stack, drawing on specialists where needed while keeping a clear view of the complete system.

•     The ability to turn competing requirements into clear technical priorities and explain trade-offs to engineers, product leads and business stakeholders.

•     Excellent oral and written communication, and the independence to take ownership, challenge proposals constructively and help others make progress when requirements are unclear.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience with platform migrations and with regulated software.

What you’ll do

You will set the technical direction for how data platforms, pipelines, integrations and AI applications fit together, and help the teams around you deliver it.

•     Define and evolve the architecture across data platforms, pipelines, integrations and AI applications, making clear decisions about how the components fit together.

•     Work with the AI and data team to translate business priorities into a technical roadmap.

•     Support the move to Databricks, including decisions on data modelling, processing, access and how downstream applications consume quality data.

•     Identify shared needs across initiatives and decide where reusable capabilities justify investment and where a simpler, local approach is enough.

•     Help engineers make sound design choices through technical discussions, architecture and code reviews, contributing directly to implementation and troubleshooting where needed.

•     Build practical engineering standards for testing, deployment, observability and maintainability, and make sure AI evaluations and data quality checks come with the traceability and evidence that GxP software requires.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Quality AI & Data, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working.

Your scope is global across Novo Quality processes. You will manage relationships with end users, engineers, product leads, IT and platform owners, and senior management across functions, units and geographies. You will resolve technical dependencies, reconcile competing needs and secure agreement on priorities, trade-offs and next steps, so work keeps moving with clarity. You will also develop engineers through feedback, shared problem-solving and clear explanations of your technical decisions. The position is based in Ballerup, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will have the independence to act within your scope, and the trust to take ownership and make your voice heard. You will work on complex problems at the forefront of AI and data technology, grow alongside colleagues through technical challenge and shared problem-solving, and help improve how the department works, simplifying ways of working and the user experience. Clear performance expectations will help you deliver your best work and be recognised for it.

Join us in this role where you’ll take a leading role in monitoring, triaging, and resolving OT and SCADA incidents across global wind assets. You’ll coordinate incident response across disciplines, drive root cause analysis, and strengthen operational resilience to ensure safe, secure, and reliable energy production. As part of our 24/7 operational setup, you’ll also join an on-duty rotation for one week each month, giving you the opportunity to take ownership when it matters most and help keep our assets running safely and reliably around the clock.

**Welcome to OT Guard & Service Management

**You’ll be part of OT Guard & Service Management where you, together with your colleagues, will support offshore and onshore assets by ensuring stable, secure, and compliant OT and SCADA operations across regions and time zones. You’ll collaborate closely with control rooms, cybersecurity, engineering teams, and suppliers to manage incidents and maintain high operational standards.

As a team, we we collaborate closely, act with integrity, and share knowledge openly to deliver safe, resilient, and high‑performing operations, even in high‑pressure situations.

**

• performing root cause analysis and documenting preventive actions to reduce repeat incidents

• conducting remote diagnostics and coordinating field or supplier interventions when required

• remain structured and calm when handling incidents in changing operational conditions
